meta.notes: DRAFT, design-shape data (design/ORISON_DIALOGUE_DRAFTS_2026-10-22.md). Threshold conversation; no case, no resolution flags. Teresa notices triage, dosage, shift handoff, pulse, who is still standing. Clipped under pressure, expansive only after danger; imperatives practical. Comic engine: treating the supernatural as the least urgent item on an impossible round. Never luxuriates in diagnosis. She was on the custody ward the night Price died; the alarm was not hers; she does not know Mina's part and Mina does not know hers. The Vales' hours do not overlap by design. She knocks once on 1A before every shift.

tv_open.line: Boots off or stand on the mat; I sleep in here. The bell. Yes. It rings with the breaker out. I've pulled the fuse, I've had the wire off the wall, it rings. I've got forty minutes before I leave for a ward where bells ring for a reason, so if you're going to look at it, look.

I've answered every one since as if it were.

tv_knock.line: Once. To hear her answer. She always answers; she'd answer a knock from the grave and correct its timing. I've never gone in. If I went in she'd give me tea and I'd have to be a person for twenty minutes, and I've a ward. ... That's not why. I don't know why. One knock. It's enough to know she's standing.

tv_mina.line: She's a grown woman with a desk. ... Seventy minutes. You've timed it. Yes. I'm out before she's down and she's up before I'm back, and we've lived one floor apart the way we lived under one roof: she leaves notes, I read them when I'm too tired to answer. She learnt to write things down because I was never awake to hear them. I know that. I've known it since she was six.

tv_cam.line: Ortiz. 4C. The courier. ... Our ward sends second reminders when the first's been ignored, and they're ignored by people who'd rather be moving than sitting in a chair being told something. I'll not say what for; it's his. But I'll stop him on the stair, which he'll hate, and I'll say 'go,' which he'll hate more.
